name: Nujuma, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve
positioning: Villa resort in the Ummahat Islands of the Red Sea, with overwater and beachfront villas, a star-gazing focus and diving
best_for: Travelers who want stargazing and diving on a Red Sea island
Guests who want a private-pool villa over the water or on the sand

facts.text: The villas were designed by Foster + Partners and are inspired by seashells.
Villas are either floating above the water or set on the sand.
Each villa has panoramic windows, open living space, a sea-view pool and a telescope for stargazing.
The Royal Nujuma Villa is the resort's most expansive accommodation.
Sita has a French-style patisserie and a Levantine restaurant with moment-prepared hummus and a central clay oven.
Tabrah is a seafood restaurant that interprets Saudi Arabia's fishing tradition.
Maia is a bar focused on astronomy, with mocktails inspired by the night sky.
Neyrah Spa has sea-facing treatment rooms, outdoor treatment cabins, yoga pavilions, vitality and lap pools, a hammam and a fitness center.
Galaxea Dive Center lets guests learn to dive, earn a certification and join diving excursions.
The Conservation House is a bridge to Saudi Arabia's marine life, history and heritage.

highlights.text: A resident astronomy expert leads stargazing and storytelling for guests.
Each villa has a telescope for stargazing, alongside panoramic windows and a sea-view pool.
Galaxea Dive Center lets guests learn to dive, earn a certification and join diving excursions.
Maia is a bar focused on astronomy, with mocktails inspired by the night sky.

considerations.text: Guests fly into Red Sea International Airport and transfer by seaplane or yacht from Red Sea Global's seaport.
WhataHotel notes the location is extremely remote and the pricing is ultra-premium.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Nujuma, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, Saudi Arabia
